name: ssdeep
why: Fuzzy piecewise hashing reveals similarity between files, a real door into malware analysis and forensics.

brief.what_it_is: ssdeep is a command-line program, with a companion library (libfuzzy), for computing context triggered piecewise hashes (CTPH), also called fuzzy hashes. You feed it files and it produces fuzzy hash strings. Those hashes can then be compared to estimate how similar two inputs are. The homepage says CTPH can match inputs that share sequences of identical bytes in the same order, even when the bytes between those sequences differ in content and length. The homepage does not spell out the exact output format or comparison syntax.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames the problem as identifying almost identical files, which ordinary cryptographic hashes cannot do because changing one byte changes the whole hash. It points to the Digital Investigation paper "Identifying almost identical files using context triggered piecewise hashing" as the full explanation. It also says ssdeep is widely used for simple identification, for example in the Basic Properties section of VirusTotal.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage gives only a high-level description. Hashes are computed piecewise, with boundaries set by content (the context-triggered part), so shared byte runs produce matching pieces even when the surrounding bytes differ. The complete mechanism is in the linked paper, which the homepage did not reproduce.
brief.install_notes: Available as a package on Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian, EPEL for CentOS and other RHEL-based distros, Arch Linux (community repository, no manual compile needed), and FreeBSD Ports (security/ssdeep, compile required). Windows has a 32-bit binary package on the GitHub project page, tested on Windows 7 and Windows 10 version 1703. Other *nix systems need a source build from GitHub using GNU Autotools. No accounts, hardware, or runtimes are mentioned on the homepage.
brief.standout: ssdeep is the long-standing de facto fuzzy hashing tool. The homepage says it remains a primary choice despite newer "better fuzzy hashes" because it is fast, claimed to be about twice as fast as TLSH. Its wide adoption, including in VirusTotal, makes it a common reference point in malware triage and forensics.
brief.status: Quiet. The homepage names 2.14.1 as the latest version, released 2017-11-07, and the changelog highlights are from that release. Tsukasa OI is listed as the current maintainer. I could not see commit history or a recent release, so I cannot confirm recent activity.
brief.caveats: Official Windows binaries are 32-bit only. Other platforms need a source build if their distribution does not package ssdeep. The speed comparison with TLSH and the claim that hashes are a de facto standard are the project's own statements. The GitHub README fetch returned only the word "README", so I could not check commands, usage, or the project's own install and run instructions. The Quick Start and manpage links were not followed because the homepage did not give their URLs. License is GPL v2 or later, for both the program and the library.
